findings.observed_upstream: Eligibility searches actual held objects against actor/body and local context, selects a typed use, and downstream use consumes/spends stock and applies the effect. findings.title: Action-specific door traps feed water into material-aware inventory consequences
findings.observed_upstream: xNetHack getdoortrap chooses a door hazard from level-eligible traps deterministically using door coordinates, level ledger and birthday (trap.c:7024-7059). doortrapped receives actor, touched body part/object, action and pre/post timing (7061-7092); for a WATER_BUCKET post-trigger on opening, breaking or untrapping, it announces a splash and passes the touching player or monster inventory to water_damage_chain (7230-7253). water_damage applies item-specific rules for grease, towels, nested/waterproof containers, scroll/book damage, potion dilution/transformation, and rust erosion, with luck/RNG exceptions and observable messages (4899-5049). The reviewed NetHack pin has water-damage helpers but no doortrapped/WATER_BUCKET symbols in src/trap.c: xNetHack adds a sampled action-specific trigger layer around related base-game water item behavior. This does not imply identical source.
findings.inference: Observed from the pinned xNetHack files and compared by symbol search/read against the pinned NetHack src/trap.c. Inference: transferable design is an action/body-part-specific environmental hazard that reaches carried stock through item function/material rules and provides evidence through visible item outcomes. No code was executed and no YAIR implementation is claimed.
findings.original_yair_example: Original proposal: a wind-up cistern at the Glasshouse archive sprays mineral mist when someone forces its pressure handle. A player carrying an exposed paper route loses its readable edge, while a wax-sealed map stays legible; a nearby apprentice can infer the mechanism only after observing a consequence. Author it as a fixed command with explicit inputs and known evidence when existing YAIR effects suffice; persistent damage state is needed only if the content requires it.

Current generic item state is count/key, with no generic wetness/material-damage/protection record or item-function/observation registry. Missing is an item-condition or affordance binding only when selected content cannot be represented by fixed existing facts/effects; there is no absent generic command executor.

Distinct value is content-authored physical item state/interference and observation mapping, not another simulation framework. findings.title: Mastery changes an actual function
findings.observed_upstream: Talent rank changes callable behavior: Manathrust switches bolt to beam at rank 3; Death Dance adds a conditional bleed at rank 3. At use, ActorTalents checks cooldown, calls the module actor pre-use rules and talent-specific on_pre_use before invoking action; postUseTalent applies declared stamina/mana/etc and game energy only when the action returns success, then ActorTalents starts cooldown. The concrete talent action applies the target effect (hit-gated stun, rank-gated bleed, or bolt/beam projection). Sustained activation stores its callback return and deactivation reverses owned temporary/resource effects. Actor-owned talent levels, cooldowns and sustain records are initialized from actor fields; the engine savefile contract documents recursive serialization of contained game objects.
findings.inference: A useful YAIR technique can mature by gaining a new supported operation/target shape or conditional follow-through while keeping the source, requirements and meaningful costs explicit. That creates distinct mastery from simply increasing output.
findings.original_yair_example: Proposal: a locally taught glassblower's calibration faculty starts as a paid one-item alignment action; established mastery permits paired alignment only when the owned jig, co-located mentor and clean glass are available; mature mastery can detect a stress line and report it to the workshop knowledge owner. The added operation is authored; this is not ToME content or a canonical YAIR balance decision.
findings.current_owner_evidence: simulation.powers already stores ownership/mastery and command preview gates execution, cooldown, world and model limits; simulation effects apply typed costs/results; energy_resources owns fuel/strain; capabilities queries source-qualified functions. Functional consumers are individually authored (skills, encounter, route and crafting). Missing integration is not cost/cooldown plumbing in YAIR: those generic typed command owners exist. The missing guarantee is a specific selected consumer binding each mastery band to a real outcome. Native battle does not automatically execute arbitrary simulation power definitions.

findings.title: Risk and execution blockers have actual consequences

upstream_evidence.lines: manual source read; spell-specific lines not used as sole evidence

findings.observed_upstream: Spell success reflects trained spell/school skill, intelligence, armor/shield, spell difficulty and status modifiers. The command checks that casting is possible before spending a turn. Failed execution and some penance states have real miscast consequences, and failure severity is exposed from the same chance/difficulty factors.
findings.inference: YAIR can make a risky extraordinary action a legible decision by quoting exact blockers, costs and authored risk before commitment, then applying any failure consequence through its existing outcome/effect owners. Risk is not a free narrative label or an automatic source of observation.
findings.original_yair_example: Proposal: a player who learned a pressure-sense pulse can preview its current strain/fuel cost and whether a sealed wall or calm body is supported; a noisy environment may make the authored reading unreliable, with failure adding fatigue and no clue. Only explicitly witnessed evidence can enter directed knowledge. Possession of the faculty alone grants no observation or report.

findings.observed_upstream: Possession is an explicit corpse-gated form transition with a player-level eligibility cap, body-dependent attacks/spells/stats/resistances/equipment, prior-body decay risk, and a low-health random ejection risk. The current body key is saved by the game and form changes recalculate derived state; body history is separately serialized. findings.inference: A YAIR body or borrowed-form route should model actual acquired body identity, functional advantages, compatibility and host liabilities at the owning actor, while keeping observation, learning, source ownership and active execution as separate facts. NPC evolution can be a local authored advancement on that NPC's own history, not player possession or a global level-scaling rule.

A consenting glasshouse technician might develop a different instrument-dependent condition after funded work. These examples do not assert current YAIR possession or body switching.

findings.title: Bound stock-aware work and profession decisions to an authored local policy
findings.observed_upstream: DFHack workflow protects repeat jobs and suspends/resumes production around per-item target/gap rules; its docs distinguish this convenience from more expressive native workorders. Autolabor presents three explicit assignment modes, ranks eligible workers by skill and policy, keeps upper/lower worker bounds, saves mode, and warns the legacy approach may disable modern work detail behavior or produce poor assignments. CDDA faction_mission's definition loader exposes an authored set of skill/risk/time/position/item alternatives/effects for specific mission types. Evennia's ScriptBase persists timed repeats as part of its always-running multiplayer server.
findings.inference: These are three different layers: production stock maintenance, workforce routing, and authored mission data. YAIR has finite one-off site phases, exact inventory/job effects and repeat programs, but no min/max stock-band consumer and no general labor-auction consumer. It should add only an explicitly selected local stock policy; automatic whole-cast job assignment would be a new system and is not implied by current foundations.
findings.original_yair_example: Second connected proposal: an optional Village workshop policy can keep a small band of Prepared survey kits by asking the named craftsman to repeat one eligible, already-authored recipe only below its lower target and pause above its upper target. The notebook can report observed shortage or blocked inputs with who noticed them. Disablement stops starting work, leaves a paid job's frozen due time and materials intact, and records no free stock. This would add bounded stock-band selection to the existing finite program/site-project paths, not generic worker reassignment. It remains a proposal, not playable behavior.

findings.title: An authored mixed-activity itinerary is the queue pattern worth borrowing
observed_upstream: The Lloyd queue has ordered current and next lists. A committed list item runs for a bounded loop count; each tick advances its action, and completion moves the cursor onward (actions.js 13-103).

Before running the next item, the scheduler checks its allowed count, current zone and canStart condition; an ineligible item is skipped while its row receives an error reason (actions.js 106-137). Each action's cost/time is estimated from its declared stats, and queue totals are recomputed from remaining actions (actions.js 214-253).
The action definitions distinguish regular, progress, limited, and multipart actions, with unique per-action data and multi-segment completion behavior (actionList.js 17-73, 110-151).

The Omsi pin has separate action and action-list blobs despite the shared README blob. Its top-level action-list comments describe typed progress, limited-use, and multipart actions, but this review does not assert identical runtime behavior from matching labels alone.
inference: The transferable pattern is a player-authored sequence with a per-step boundary: forecast known duration/costs, then re-evaluate legal access and actual means when each next command is about to begin. YAIR should stop and expose the blocked step instead of copying Idle Loops' skip-ahead behavior, because a later step may rely on work that never happened.
Idle Loops' town index and action-specific tick state are game-specific. Importing them would duplicate YAIR's command registry, job scheduler and current world/location owners.
findings.original_yair_example: Proposal only: prepare a field itinerary with 'observe the washed trail', 'ask the carpenter to pack one kit', then 'practice the brace'. Show the predicted work and known costs. Each later step rechecks current locality, discovery, participant availability and stock. If the logs are spent elsewhere before packing begins, stop with the exact blocked step; do not spend hidden resources or skip into a different world. It remains one ordinary realm and does not advance while the player is absent.

findings.title: Mentor specialization is useful as a consequence pattern, not a task engine to import
observed_upstream: Arcanum Task gates use by timer and general task eligibility; active tasks accrue rate-scaled elapsed progress and completion increments the task value before notifying listeners and resetting progress (task.js 209-262).

Runnable tasks serialize item, target and progress; completion applies the selected item-to-target interaction, emits a task-done event, and revival restores the target reference and resumes item use (runnable.js 11-16, 65-70, 90-113).

Arcanum Testing's distinct mentor module gates a one-time master specialization on authored progress facts and changes different power rate/capacity or home/job modifiers (masterspecs.json 5-19, 22-54, 57-89, 92-120).
inference: The useful design relation is a meaningful mentor choice whose eligibility reflects what the player actually did and whose effects touch a real source, home service, or ordinary task. It should not become a generic task-timer subsystem or copy Arcanum's text/IDs.

Most infrastructure is already covered by YAIR frozen paid jobs, power/faculty ownership, directed knowledge and native XP integration. The candidate gap is an authored content link from earned local discovery to a mentor's distinct functional lesson, not a new progression ledger.

findings.title: Keep civilization job economies and offline/reset rules as separate design boundaries
observed_upstream: Evolve tech entries declare prerequisites, sometimes a species condition, real resource costs, and effects such as displaying a resource or granting a technology era step; techList filters by authored path (tech.js 18-129, 15698-15715).

Evolve profession projections compute worker output using species traits, current technologies, biome/buildings, and government; professor/scientist descriptions are tied to these shared economy facts (jobs.js 273-315, 413-445). This is not evidence that each projection line directly mutates saved stock.

Progress Knight Quest's repository description names five prestige layers. Its inspected offline path caps elapsed catch-up to one hour, runs batches of 200 ticks with brief UI yields, and stops processing on death (offline.js 7-12, 35-72, 79-102).
inference: Evolve illustrates a materially distinct collective technological progression fantasy: population assignments produce resources, then research choices consume those resources to reveal new capabilities. Current YAIR simulation specializes in person-owned actors, commands, work reservations, sources and local world facts; a collectively assigned population/economy would need an actual new producer/consumer contract.

Progress Knight Quest's offline tick replay and five-layer reset structure are incompatible design decisions for current scope. Neither should be copied as a convenience under the current explicit played-time/world-absence policy or one-prestige milestone.
findings.original_yair_example: Proposal for a later distinct campaign concept only: a frontier settlement may assign two named local workers to a survey office; a separately committed research lesson then consumes actual shared material through an explicitly owned settlement stock adapter and grants an earned source to a consenting trainee. Existing simulation jobs reserve actor-owned costs, sites and participants and settle frozen effects; simulation effects write real inventory, knowledge, powers, source/faculty and progress owners (108-170; simulation_effects.js 144-244).
Current costs are constrained to real typed resources/items/vitals/transfers/custody/energy; saved person jobs and world records are validated against actual owners (90-98, 191-237).
Current advancement uses the joined played clock, bounded boundary processing and explicit frozen local-world time during absence; browser-closed catch-up is not an implicit feature (118-124).

symbols: What does QuestJS code look like?

findings.observed_upstream: Attack.createAttack selects a default or requested skill, checks activity and skill-specific usability before producing an attack, resolves primary and secondary targets, and builds the attack from the skill, weapon, actor, held objects, room, and active effects. findings.title: NPC agendas encode finite turn-by-turn duties and a guarded return to the starting routine
findings.observed_upstream: The agenda module authors guard-item, patrol, walk-to, and antagonize actions as sequential agenda entries. Patrol advances through a finite route; walk-to resolves a room/object destination and moves one step toward it, returning incomplete until arrival. Guard setup stores an initial action/location for later resumption. NPC endTurn selects among guard handler, current agenda when not paused/suspended, or hostile-target attack, then processes its event. agendaRestart rebuilds a return-to-origin plus original action pair unless settings are absent or resumption is disabled. Comments explicitly mark patrol/walk-to attack behavior as future work, so this is a finite routine/return pattern, not a general autonomous planner. The default save path serializes each world object and accepts string arrays, so a string-array agenda cursor can be saved; generic saveLoadExclude filters object-valued attributes and get/set save paths restore only encoded types. Thus the agenda sequence can survive through the default object serializer, while agendaOriginalSettings is a plain object and is omitted by default unless an author supplies a custom serialization route. This is a source-level save-path reading, not a save/reload execution.
findings.inference: These sequencing, pause/suspension, movement, and return mechanics are observed. Mapping such a routine into a YAIR finite actor controller or planned job is an inference. No QuestJS routine or game content is present in YAIR and no behavior is claimed as implemented by this review. Persistence qualification: string-array agenda data is accepted by the generic serializer, while a plain-object original-settings snapshot is excluded by default. Whether a particular game customizes this remains game-specific and was not executed.
findings.original_yair_example: Proposal only: a roaming lamp-mender has a finite evening duty to collect two actual wick bundles from the storehouse, repair one beacon if the storm warning is active, leave a note for the watch, and return to his bench. Player intervention can pause the route; whether he resumes depends on the authored obligation and the supplies actually remaining. This example proposes no new campaign or universal daily-life rule.

Boundary advancement visits due controllers, advances their due time, checks authored action eligibility, and submits one supported action (317-380); jobs already have preview, commit, pause, resume, and cancel routes (49-207).

Effects can spend/transfer actual simulation inventory, change location/facts/conditions, add memories/causes, and spawn people; seeded event resolution is separate and deterministic by saved seed/id (simulation_effects.js 77-100, 144-211; simulation_resolution.js 4-41).

findings.title: Scenario WML joins discovery-gated encounters, a unit-bound reward, named recalls, and a campaign transition gate
findings.observed_upstream: Scenario 02 starts with named hero recall calls for Nym, Garak, and Zhul and advertises the single next scenario. A scout moving within radius 8 of the scorpion nest triggers a warning and places the encounter; a non-scout entering radius 3 triggers the ambush directly. Defeating the last scuttler drops a ring and installs a one-time move event. The player can assign the unit-bound object that grants hydration immunity to the unit reaching the drop, or defer taking it; the event and location record are cleared on acceptance. A separate ogre path has scout-revealed and close-range ambush cases, while defeating the leader is mandatory before Kaleh can win by reaching the north edge. Victory carries 40 percent gold into the next scenario. Scenario 03's prestart recalls named heroes including the Dust Devil; its own turn-1 logic also recalls troops conditionally. The source scenario thus uses stable actor identity/recall plus local WML variables and event removal, while carryover and unit object effects are the visible reward/persistence routes. The C++ carryover owner makes the persistence boundary explicit: carryover stores recall units as config records because live units may depend on resources unavailable between scenarios; it removes board coordinates/hidden state when collecting the recall record, serializes the unit records and scenario variables, and transfers recall units, recruits, gold, variables, RNG and next-scenario identity into the next level/save config. This confirms the campaign-level retained-unit/variable path in source without executing the game.
findings.inference: The scenario WML and C++ carryover serialization/transfer paths above are observed at the pinned source. The claim that the ring object modification remains attached after recall is still an inference from unit-bound object assignment plus retained unit config; this review did not trace the object serializer payload in a running scenario or execute save/load. This is not a full campaign or engine review. The source scenario calls out one next_scenario; its local encounter alternatives are not alternate campaign destinations.
findings.original_yair_example: Proposal only: on a native frontier walk, a watch scout who spends a real field ration and has the required observation skill may expose a wind-carved cistern before the party enters its hazard radius. Resolving the encounter can earn one named travel charm assigned to an actual consenting carrier; either route leads to the same next local chapter, with a recorded fact changing the arrival support.
